intro: A randomization test asks whether a group difference is unusual under exchanged labels. Supplied reorderings make each null statistic inspectable.
task: Evaluate a two-sided difference-of-means randomization test using supplied full permutations and a plus-one Monte Carlo correction.
requirements: values is a length-n vector, n>=2. group_size is an integer in [1,n-1]. The original first group_size values form group A and the rest form B.
permutations is a nonempty matrix with n columns. Each row must be an exact permutation of integer positions 0..n-1; rows may repeat.

For each reordered vector, subtract the mean of its last n-group_size entries from that of its first group_size entries. Return {"observed": original_difference, "null": statistic vector, "p_value": (1+count(abs(null)>=abs(observed)))/(1+b)}.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Validate that each row reorders all positions exactly once, then use its first group_size positions as group A.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Count null statistics at least as extreme in absolute magnitude, including equality, before applying the plus-one correction.

explanation: Under an exchangeability assumption, relabeling observations generates a null comparison. Recompute both group means after each reordering, including when group sizes differ.
This exercise uses a plus-one Monte Carlo correction, so finite null draws never give zero p-value. Exhaustive exact permutation tests can use another convention; the contract fixes this one.
